title: Comparing surgical intervention versus infiltration of cytokine autologous rich serum (proteins derived from the patient's own blood) for the treatment of tennis elbow.
official: Randomized Clinical Trial for the Treatment of Lateral Epicondylitis with Debridement Arthroscopic Versus Cytokine-Rich Autologous Serum. (SARC)
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the effectiveness of SARC compared to the arthroscopic resection in the reduction of pain in the medium term (6 months) in patients with chronic lateral epicondylitis.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Over 18 years
2. Patients who present persistent pain (VAS > 5) at the level of lateral epicondyle of at least 3 months’ duration.
3. Patients with a confirmed diagnosis of chronic lateral epicondylitis with some complementary diagnostic test such as ECO or MRI.
4. Availability to be able to follow up on the protocol of the study up to 24 months.
5. Patients with the ability to understand the study information and give informed consent.
6. Patients who sign the informed consent.
7. Normal hematological parameters.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Local infection present.
2. Coagulation deficiency or abnormalities.
3. Thrombocytopenia.
4. Treatment with anticoagulants.
5. Difficulty understanding and following study procedures.
6. Participation in a clinical trial with medications.
7. Patients who have received treatment with infiltrations of corticosteroids in the same area in the last 4 months.
8. Patients who have received treatment with growth factors, PRP, cytokines or new pharmacological treatments in it area in the last 12 months.
9. Pregnancy or breastfeeding.
10. Neoplastic Disease.
11. Patients undergoing treatment with immunosuppressants (medical assessment).
12. Patients undergoing arthroscopic surgery of the same elbow.
13. Active liver disease.
14. States of immunosuppression or immunodeficiencies.
